Choosing a PSX stock broker

Your broker is the gateway to PSX. The “best” firm is the one that is properly licensed, charges transparently, lets you fund and withdraw safely, and gives you statements you can trust. Fee cards go stale quickly, so treat this as a checklist you verify yourself.

By PSX Tracker · Updated 23 September 2026

Start with licensing, not ads

Confirm the broker is authorised to offer PSX trading through official PSX or SECP information, not only a sponsored social post.

Understand how your shares are held (typically via CDC sub-account arrangements your broker sets up) and keep login security under your control — never share OTPs.

Costs you should verify on today’s schedule

Ask for or download the current commission structure, CDC or custody-related charges, and any account maintenance or inactivity fees.

Compare total cost for the way you trade (frequent small orders vs occasional larger ones). A headline commission can look cheap until other line items appear on the contract note.

Save a copy of the fee schedule you were shown when you opened the account.

App quality and order confidence

You will use the app under time pressure. Check how clear order tickets are, whether you can see open orders and fills, and how contract notes are delivered.

If the app is confusing on day one, it will be worse in a volatile session.

Funding, withdrawals and support

Test deposit instructions with a small amount first. Confirm withdrawal timelines and whether support answers before you move a large balance.

Prefer funding from a bank account in your own name and the broker’s published client account details.

Statements and portfolio tracking

Good brokers make it easy to download trade history. Clean exports reduce errors when you import into PSX Tracker or reconcile manually.

If exports are painful, budget extra time for bookkeeping — or choose a broker that respects your need for records.

This guide is educational only. It is not investment, tax, legal or religious advice. Rules, fees and tax rates change — confirm details with your broker, SECP/PSX sources, FBR guidance and qualified advisors before you act.

Licensing before convenience

Start from the register, not from an advertisement. A firm that can broker PSX trades is registered for that activity. SECP and PSX publish ways to confirm a broker. A WhatsApp contact who offers “guaranteed lots” and asks you to transfer money to a personal account is not a shortcut. It is a reason to stop.

The brand on the app store is not the same check. Read the legal name on the account-opening form and match it to the registered name. If the form and the advertisement disagree, use the form’s name for the register search.

You can hold accounts at more than one broker. Many investors do, then struggle to see one portfolio. A tracker that records the broker on each trade lets you keep the books separate and still look at the combined holdings. The broker’s own app remains the place you place orders.

What the fee card actually contains

Commission is the line people compare, and it is rarely the only line. A schedule can also include a tax on the commission, CDC or clearing charges, and other regulatory amounts. The names and the rates change. Print or save the schedule on the day you open the account, and save it again when the broker emails a revision.

A lower commission on a huge notional can still be a poor deal if withdrawals are slow or statements are unusable. A slightly higher commission with a clean CSV and a same-day contract note can be cheaper in the hours you will spend reconstructing a year of trades.

Do not publish someone else’s fee table as if it were permanent, and do not trust one you memorized last year. The trade-cost calculator on this site adds the commission, the tax on that commission, and a CDC amount you type from your own schedule. It does not store a broker’s current card.

Funding, withdrawals, and whose account it is

Client money should move on the broker’s published funding instructions, into an account in the broker’s client-money name, from a bank account in your name. If a representative asks you to use their personal wallet “just this once,” refuse.

Try a small withdrawal before you need a large one. The test is whether the money returns to the same bank account, in a stated number of days, without a new set of unofficial charges. Note the date and the amount in your own ledger so the cash balance stays explainable.

Joint accounts, company accounts, and accounts for someone else have their own paperwork. Do not place a relative’s trades inside your login and hope to sort the beneficial owner later. The CDC sub-account name is part of the record.

Statements you can actually reconcile

Before you fund a large amount, ask how you will download contract notes, a period statement, and a holdings list. A PDF that you can save is the minimum. A CSV or spreadsheet export saves a weekend when you import history into a tracker.

Check one sample statement for the fields you need: trade date, symbol, buy or sell, quantity, price, commission, and other charges. If the symbol is missing or the date is ambiguous, you will mis-key the ledger. Day-first and month-first dates are a common way to land a trade in the wrong month.

After the first ten trades, reconcile. Open quantity in the tracker should match the broker. Cash should match deposits, withdrawals, buys, sells, dividends, and fees, with transfers between your own portfolios left out of the cash story. If it does not match, fix the entry while you still remember the trade.

App quality is a safety feature

You will place orders on a phone, in a moving market. An app that hides the order type, the limit price, or the symbol you are about to buy is a source of errors, not a convenience. Practice with a small limit order and confirm the contract note the same day.

Support matters on the day a deposit does not show or a symbol looks wrong. Note the hours, the language, and whether you can reach a person. A community forum is not the broker’s complaint process.

PSX Tracker does not choose a broker and does not receive your order. Use this guide as a checklist, confirm the firm on the official register, and keep the contract notes. The portfolio app starts after the fill exists.

Common questions

What should I compare?

Licensing, how you fund and withdraw, the app you will actually use, costs, and whether you can export statements.

Are published fee tables permanent?

No. Brokers change schedules. Confirm the current schedule with the broker before you treat a figure as exact.

Does PSX Tracker replace a broker?

No. It keeps the ledger. The broker holds the account and executes trades.
